scalars.scalar_value: Bachelors degree from a Physical Therapy institution accredited by the APTA.

items.item_text: Current California Physical Therapy license or eligible for same
1-3 years experience as a licensed Physical Therapist in a hospital setting
Bachelors degree from a Physical Therapy institution accredited by the APTA.
Masters degree from a Physical Therapy institution accredited by the APTA.
Doctorate of Science from a Physical Therapy institution accredited by the APTA.

Evaluates and treats all patient diagnoses comprehensively, and identifies appropriate treatment plan and goals consistent with physician's referral, patient's diagnosis, abilities and age -using objective, measurable data, within departmental policy timelines.
Communicates professionally and effectively (SBAR format) with the entire health care team (rehab, nursing, physicians, case managers) to effectively provide the best possible care for the patient.

Communicates with Director and supervisor effectively, and in a timely manner, regarding any issues, requests or ideas. Completes and forwards all required hospital and department forms, such as timecards, time-off requests, projects, without need for reminders.

All required Medical record documentation is timely, complete, legible and compliant with all departmental standards and regulatory guidelines, including the justification for skilled Physical Therapy need.

Consistently maintains productivity level at or above department standard and demonstrates excellent time management, including adjusting schedule as needed to complete assignments ,communicating with the team and using downtime effectively.
